implementation.owner: packages/golden-ui/components/common/Slider.svelte and slider-value.ts own pointer/keyboard geometry and declared step-grid presentation. NumberEditor owns typed Parameter interaction and uses existing session preview/intent/edit-session contracts. time-value.ts owns stored-unit clock presentation only; backend/domain constraints and authored history remain authoritative.
implementation.gestures: Pointer capture replaces document mouse listeners and cursor-hiding state. One owned pointer, fractional-step accumulation, bounds/grid origin, fine Alt/coarse Shift, Escape/pointercancel/lost-capture restoration and unmount cleanup are shared across consumers. Start/end callbacks take no value argument, preserving zero-start vector grouping. Keyboard Arrow/Page/Home/End and accessible slider names/ranges share the same constrained values.
implementation.time: Plain time uses relative steps so wide millisecond bounds stay usable; declared step wins, otherwise one millisecond per pixel. The explicit bounded slider remains available. Stored/API units remain ms or seconds. Formatting infers precision from both step and current value, preserving unstepped fractions and fine raw-ms steps. Decimal clock parts are parsed once in the authored unit to avoid extra floating-point rounding. Clock presentation supports up to12 fractional second digits; existing integer-ms controls still display three.
implementation.drafts: NumberEditor reads existing session Parameter previews before committed graph data. Accepted values remain visible across held graph publication without another acknowledgement owner. Invalid/rejected clock or range text restores the displayed value; read-only fields now expose their native readonly attribute as well as existing admission guards.
implementation.unchanged: No Rust source, product schema, generated DTO, authored settings or native rendering change. M13/11's564-test backend/strict/generated/native fade evidence is reused only for that unchanged scope. No additional expensive Rust test/lint cycle is claimed for this UI-only slice.

software.focused: Six time/grid tests cover seconds/ms unit roundtrips, integer milliseconds, sub-ms precision, unstepped fractional values, fine steps, malformed input, one-sided/unbounded stepped dragging and nonzero grid origins/bounds.
software.format: Touched source/fixtures/docs use repository Prettier; Node syntax, owning diff checks, root and golden_core cargo fmt pass. Initial compiler/rune warnings were corrected; no new warning is retained.
